gates.evidence: AOL news browsing is a general-interest activity for a broad audience.
The reward is ad-free browsing time, not a click, install, or cash reward.
The offer uses gain-framed copy: 'Go Ad-Free for 15 Minutes'.
The user must tap the 'Ad-Free Sprint' button, and Simula RWD units require a clear opt-in.
The offer clearly states 'Play a 15-second game' to receive '15 minutes of ad-free browsing'.
The offer includes a 'No thanks' button and allows the user to continue browsing.
The offer appears in the feed as a button; there is no AI streaming conversation to interrupt.
The proposal limits eligibility to non-paying users.

scores.evidence: The reward of 15 minutes of ad-free news is a highly valued relief from AOL's frequent Taboola ads, but 15 minutes is a relatively short window for a browsing session.
The 'Ad-free Sprint' is framed in-world as a sprint with the 'AOL News Editor', which fits the news environment well without disrupting article reading.
The offer is time-boxed to 15 minutes and capped at 3 uses per day, ensuring it remains a supplement rather than a replacement for any potential subscription.
The cost to serve is zero as this relies on ad suppression. Revenue per view is captured through the rewarded ad view, providing a positive return.
The 'Home News Feed' (s02) is a core component of the app; most DAU will encounter Taboola units frequently.
The proposal requires technical implementation of ad-suppression logic for Taboola units; integration via RWD/SIM-RWD is standard.
The proposal uses AOL-specific UI elements (Taboola ad units, feed headers) and introduces a thematic 'News Editor' partner.
The proposal explicitly sets a cap of 3 per day and a 60-minute cooldown.
KPIs are clearly defined, and the proposal plans for a user-level holdout experiment.

requiredChanges: Clarify the trigger definition: the proposal contradicts itself by suggesting both an auto-trigger ('After user scrolls past 3 native Taboola ad units') and a button-based entry point (ne1). Clarify that the offer is exclusively via the button (ne1) and remove any reference to auto-scrolling triggers to ensure compliance with anti-forced-ad policies.
Correct the 'economy' section in the proposal; 'TEMU in Taboola advertising section' is an element, not an economy resource or currency. Only include legitimate app resources or scarcity anchors.
parsed.topConcern: The proposal's trigger logic is contradictory. It must strictly be a voluntary, button-initiated offer. Forced triggers based on scroll behavior (auto-triggering ads) are prohibited by AdMob and Unity policies as 'forced ads disguised as rewarded'.
